links.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy across vignette phrasing variations (characteristic vs vague symptoms, self-diagnosis framing)
links.effect: Accuracy was 92% (165/180), unaffected by patient self-diagnosis, but higher for characteristic than vague symptom descriptions.
links.quote: Accuracy was unaffected by the patient's self-diagnosis, was higher for characteristic than vague symptom, and was lower for de Quervain tendinopathy relative to other conditions.

links.outcome: Change in LLM diagnosis when randomized patient characteristics and self-diagnosis were varied
links.effect: Accuracy unaffected by self-diagnosis; model deviated from patient's diagnosis in 117 scenarios (65%), 104 (89%) aligned with intended diagnosis.
links.quote: The model deviated from the patient's proposed diagnosis in 117 scenarios (65%), of which 104 deviations (89%) appropriately aligned with the intended diagnosis.

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM diagnostic accuracy and susceptibility to anchoring/framing bias across simulated patient clinical vignettes, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
